text:
Tom: The office fern died. I think it gave us a prophetic last leaf though. RIP Fernaldo. :pensive:
Yuri: Fernaldo? nominate for sainthood. what did the leaf say?
Leah: it said 'rearrange the standing desks' in morse code if you stare long enough.
Sam: I looked. It said 'more sunlight' and maybe a grocery list.
Tom: also a tiny post-it under the pot: 'water me on Tuesdays'. I swear I never saw that before.
Maya: conspiracy: the fern was part of an internal loyalty program. You didn't hit your watering KPI.
Tom: guilty. I confess.
ops-bot: poll created: "What's our new plant mascot?" 3 options: Spider Plant; Cactus; Tiny Bonsai. React with :one: :two: :three: to vote.
Yuri: vote cactus. low maintenance, high judgment.
Leah: cactus sounds cold. bonsai for ambiance.
Sam: spider plant because it will quietly multiply and take over the finance spreadsheets.
finance-bot: note: office greenery correlated with snack spending +3%. Recommend budget allocation.
Maya: also idea: Plant Oracle. Put a small whiteboard next to it for people to ask non-binding life questions. The fern used to answer yes/no by leaf twitching.
Tom: I miss the leaf twitch. We should have a small funeral: tea, a minute of silence, and a tiny hat for Fernaldo.
Leah: I'll bring a tiny hat. Chris from Ops has spare confetti packets.
Yuri: naming ceremony required for new plant. Proposal: 'Chair of Quiet Decisions' or 'Auditor of Coffee Breaks'.
Sam: 'Auditor of Coffee Breaks' is terrifyingly accurate.
Maya: Also, let's make a 'Plant Care Rotation' calendar. Whoever misses their turn must bring cookies.
Tom: cookies are persuasive. sign me up as mourner + cookie baker.
ops-bot: reminder scheduled: 'Plant Funeral + New Plant Vote' Friday 14:00 in #random.
Leah: Also, can we have a tiny plaque that says "Fernaldo: He believed in photosynthesis"?
Maya: love it. legacy plaque + hat + tiny confetti.
Sam: if the new plant judges us, we'll know to start bringing better snacks.
Tom: agreement: charge 1 cookie tax for every missed watering.
Yuri: done. this thread is officially part of Redwood folklore. future archaeologists will find the plaque and assume we had a ceremonial cult of plants.
Tom: we'll leave them the tiny hat.
